results.title: Mahama urges global investors to consider Ghana, says country is ‘friend to all’
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama has urged investors from across the world to explore opportunities in Ghana, assuring them that the country is open to partnerships with all nations, regardless of their political or economic affiliations.

results.title: Ga Mantse commends Interior Minister for efforts to promote peace and security
results.content: The Ga Mantse, King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, has commended the Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, for his efforts to promote peace and security across Ghana.

results.title: GIPA identifies 48 investment opportunities in Upper West Region
results.content: The Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA) says it has identified 48 investment opportunities in the Upper West Region, which require millions of Ghana cedis to be harnessed.

results.title: PSDPEP scholarship students present research progress at SIF
results.content: MPhil and PhD students benefiting from scholarships under the Post-COVID-19 Skills Development and Productivity Enhancement Project (PSDPEP) have presented updates on their research at the Social Investment Fund (SIF), outlining their progress, achievements and expected outcomes.

results.title: Use budget to implement 24-hour economy in phases – Prof Bokpin
results.content: Professor Godfred Alufar Bokpin, an Economist, has proposed a phased implementation of the Government’s flagship 24-hour economy policy, backed by a dedicated yearly allocation in the national budget.

results.title: NDC clears 46 Aspirants to vie for various regional positions in Bono East
results.content: The Bono East Regional office of the National Democratic Congress has successfully vetted 46 aspirants, clearing them to vie for the various regional positions in the party.

results.title: GoldBod to help establish gold processing centres to improve traceability – Deputy Lands Minister
results.content: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) is collaborating with the government to establish gold processing centres for small-scale mining cooperatives, in a move aimed at improving the traceability of gold purchased from miners.

results.title: T-Bills on USSD: The micro-investing boom in Ghana
results.content: From the introduction of the Branchless Banking Guidelines in 2008, which paved the way for the establishment of Ghana's first mobile money service, to the widespread adoption and confidence seen today, the evolution of mobile money in Ghana has been truly remarkable.

results.title: Youth Minister inaugurates working group to advance youth development agenda
results.content: The Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment, George Opare Addo, has inaugurated the Working Group of the Ministry’s Joint Steering Committee, tasking members to support government efforts to address challenges facing young people, particularly substance abuse, while promoting skills development and youth empowerment.

results.title: Government plans permanent military camps along rivers to intensify galamsey fight
results.content: The government is planning to establish permanent military camps along selected rivers to prevent illegal miners from returning to affected areas, as it pushes back against criticism that its campaign against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, has weakened.

results.title: Sam George urges Africa to develop homegrown digital technologies
results.content: The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovation, Samuel Nartey George, has called on African countries to reduce their dependence on foreign technology by investing in homegrown digital solutions that address the continent’s unique needs and development priorities.

results.title: Government targets 70% gold recovery rate with new processing centres for small-scale miners
results.content: The government is working to establish gold processing centres for small-scale mining cooperatives, with the first facilities expected to be introduced in the first quarter of 2027 as part of efforts to improve gold recovery and reduce the environmental impact of mining.

results.title: TEWU calls for greater recognition and support for non-teaching staff in education sector
results.content: The Teachers and Educational Workers’ Union of the Trades Union Congress (TEWU of TUC Ghana) has called for greater recognition, improved working conditions and adequate support for non-teaching staff to enhance quality education delivery in the country.

results.title: Big Push will advance eco-tourism development in Bono East – Regional Minister
results.content: Francis Owusu Antwi, Bono East Regional Minister, says the execution of the government’s “Big Push” Road infrastructure initiative would boost ecotourism development in the region.

results.title: Ghana needs jobs, not more expenditure cuts – Prof Bokpin
results.content: Professor Godfred Alufar Bokpin, an Economist, has urged the government to shift from aggressive expenditure cuts to job-led growth to sustain economic stability and promote inclusive development.

results.title: Mining communities must not be left in poverty after mine closure – Zanetor
results.content: Mining communities must benefit from sustainable development and not be left with poverty and environmental degradation when mines close, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, Minister of Environment, Science and Technology, has said.

results.title: GHS develops grievance redress guidelines to improve healthcare delivery
results.content: The Ghana Health Service (GHS) has developed grievance redress guidelines to provide clear channels for addressing complaints from patients, health workers, suppliers and contractors, as part of efforts to improve healthcare delivery and strengthen public trust.

results.title: GTA engages stakeholders on animal welfare policy
results.content: The Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) is engaging stakeholders in the tourism and hospitality industry to develop a policy framework to promote responsible animal welfare practices in the sector.

results.title: Fisheries Ministry concerned over missing fishing canoe and seven crew members
results.content: The Ministry of Fisheries and Aquaculture has expressed concern over the disappearance of a fishing canoe, ‘Second Chance’, and its seven crew members, who have been missing since departing Sekondi Fishing Harbour on October 9, 2026.

results.title: Ghana develops five-year plan to advance reparations agenda
results.content: Ghana has developed a five-year action plan to advance reparations through diplomatic engagement, reparative financing and reforms to the global financial architecture.

results.title: Obuasi SHTS scandal: Gender Ministry moves to support students
results.content: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection has deployed a team to Obuasi to provide medical and psychological support to students affected by the alleged sexual abuse scandal at the Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS).

results.title: Oil rises as US orders diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid escalating tensions
results.content: Oil prices rose on Thursday as more attacks by the Houthis in Saudi ‌Arabia prompted the United States to order some diplomats and family members to leave its missions in the Kingdom.

results.title: Meta strikes deal to keep Zuckerberg in California after wealth tax concerns
results.content: Meta Platforms has struck a deal with Mark Zuckerberg to keep him in California after the CEO warned he was considering leaving the state that houses the company's headquarters if voters pass a wealth tax proposal next month.

results.title: Tesla aims to sell Cybercab robotaxis by end of year despite federal probe
results.content: Tesla ​is aiming to start selling its Cybercab robotaxis to the public by the end of this year, its ‌engineering chief said on Wednesday, even as the US auto safety agency probes the vehicles that come without manual controls, which federal regulations typically require.

results.title: Remove barriers to digital work, Bright Simons urges government
results.content: Vice-President in charge of research at IMANI Centre for Policy and Education, Bright Simons, has urged government to remove barriers that prevent ordinary Ghanaians from earning a living through digital platforms.

results.title: Meta sued in Australian class action over alleged social media harm to children
results.content: A class-action lawsuit has been filed in an Australian ​court against Meta Platforms' Facebook and Instagram ‌that alleges the social media platforms exposed children to harmful content and kept them addicted through algorithms.

results.title: Airbnb hosts can no longer make guests strip beds and wash dishes under new rules
results.content: Airbnb has changed its rules to limit what property hosts can ask guests to do—including cleaning.

results.title: ‘Who builds schools to teach people how to use WhatsApp?’ – Bright Simons
results.content: Vice-President and head of Research at the IMANI Centre for Policy and Education, Bright Simons, has urged policymakers to remove barriers that keep ordinary Ghanaians from benefiting from digital technology.

results.title: Crystal Palace urged to retire bald eagle mascot
results.content: An animal rights group is urging Crystal Palace to retire its live bald eagle mascot immediately, saying a "bright stadium filled with boisterous fans is no place for animals".

results.title: PSG’s Kvaratskhelia to undergo surgery for a ruptured ACL
results.content: Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will undergo knee surgery after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) during his side's 4-2 win over Barcelona on Tuesday.

results.title: Fernandes rounds on Carrick after Man Utd humiliation
results.content: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes turned on head coach Michael Carrick after one of the club's most humiliating nights in European history.

results.title: Solve local problems before taking on global giants — Zipline director
results.content: Ghanaian entrepreneurs should focus on solving specific local problems and build businesses around their competitive advantages instead of attempting to compete directly with established global companies, the Country Director of Zipline Ghana, Mr Daniel Kwaku Merki, has said.

results.title: ‘Ghana must not miss the AI train’ – Zipline Ghana Director
results.content: Ghana cannot afford to miss the opportunities presented by artificial intelligence (AI), the Country Director of Zipline Ghana, Daniel Kwaku Merk, has warned, saying the consequences of falling behind could last for decades or even centuries.

results.title: ‘Government is an impediment rather than an enabler’ – Bright Simons on digital platforms
results.content: Vice-President and head of Research at the IMANI Centre for Policy and Education, Bright Simons, warned that government can obstruct the digital opportunities ordinary Ghanaians rely on for work and income.

results.title: Bright Simons questions Sam George on feasibility of Ghana’s AI compute centre, cites power and water costs
results.content: Vice President of IMANI Africa, Bright Simons, has raised concerns about the feasibility of Ghana’s planned artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure, citing electricity costs, water supply and lessons from previous attempts to develop locally built digital services.

results.title: Meta fined $25bn for ‘lies’ over user data privacy
results.content: Meta, the company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp has been hit with the largest ever fine against it for its business practices.

results.title: Ghana must build its own email services to address US data concerns – Bright Simons
results.content: IMANI Centre for Policy and Education Vice-President and Head of Research Bright Simons says concerns about US access to Ghanaian data would require the country to build its own email services.

results.title: Elsinore to The Hunger Games: 12 of the best films to watch in November
results.content: From an awards-tipped role for Andrew Scott to another Hunger Games prequel, here are the films to watch at the cinema and stream at home this month.

results.title: Think about how we sign these agreements – Sam George warns over health data
results.content: Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations Minister Sam Nartey George has urged closer scrutiny of agreements involving Ghana’s health records.

results.title: ‘Real-world skill sets’ – Sam George makes case for One Million Coders programme
results.content: Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations Minister Sam Nartey George says the One Million Coders programme is designed to equip people with practical skills they can use in everyday life and business.

results.title: A case for a systematic rollout of Ghana’s new traffic law (L.I. 2519
results.content: The Ministry of Transport launched a nationwide education exercise in September 2026, with Transport Minister Joseph Bukari Nikpe acknowledging that nationwide education was “necessary to help drivers, transport operators, motor unions and other road users understand their responsibilities”. But one month of sensitization is certainly not enough time to absorb dozens of new offences and changed penalties.

results.title: Sam George outlines $270m Ghana AI investment, cites risks of feeding government data into foreign models
results.content: The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has outlined a $270 million investment in Ghana’s artificial intelligence (AI) development, with $250 million earmarked for infrastructure and computing capacity and the remaining $20 million for seed funding for an AI fund.

results.title: ‘Those who evolve and adapt will survive’ – Sam George on AI and jobs
results.content: The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, says that workers who fail to adapt to changing technology risk losing their jobs as artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes the world of work.

results.title: African mineral value addition in focus at ‘Mining in Motion Conference’
results.content: The Chief Executive Officer of the Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF), Justina Nelson, has highlighted the importance of investment, data sharing and regional cooperation in helping African countries derive greater value from their mineral resources.

results.title: ‘That is a mirage’ – Sam George on foreign cloud data-sovereignty assurances
results.content: Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations Minister Sam Nartey George has challenged assurances that agreements with foreign cloud providers guarantee control over data.

results.title: Black Maidens fight back to hold Brazil in six-goal thriller
results.content: Ghana’s Black Maidens mounted a determined fightback to hold Brazil to a pulsating 3-3 draw on Wednesday night, with Priscilla Mensah striking five minutes from time to deny the South Americans victory at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

results.title: Sam George announces national data exchange hub to connect 48 public registries
results.content: The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has announced plans to establish a national data exchange hub to connect 48 public data registries and enable seamless information sharing across government institutions.

results.title: Bleoo ’15 launches ‘Adopt a Classroom’ project to improve learning environment at Accra Academy
results.content: The 2015 Year Group of Accra Academy, popularly known as Bleoo ’15, has launched its signature ‘Adopt a Classroom’ project, an initiative aimed at renovating and modernising classrooms at the school to create a better learning environment for current and future students. The project was announced at a ceremony at the K.G. Konuah Hall of Accra Academy, where Bleoo ’15 was formally inaugurated, marking a new chapter in the year group’s commitment to alumni welfare, school development and service to its alma mater. The ‘Adopt a Classroom’ initiative seeks to mobilise support from old boys, corporate organisations and well-meaning individuals to improve classroom facilities and contribute to the school’s continued pursuit of academic excellence.

results.title: KNUST, MTN sign MoU to strengthen industry-academia collaboration and develop AI talent
results.content: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with telecommunications company MTN Ghana to strengthen industry-academia collaboration, equip students with practical skills and develop homegrown solutions to Ghana’s technological challenges.

results.title: NDC dismisses NPP claims over Nadowli 24-hour economy market, touts MP’s development record
results.content: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Nadowli-Kaleo Constituency has dismissed allegations by the New Patriotic Party (NPP) regarding proposed changes to the ongoing 24-hour economy market project, while highlighting the development record of Member of Parliament Anthony Mwinkaara Sumah.
